message.content:
You are skeptic #1. A WCAG/§4 audit of Heard's "customer-account" screen produced this finding. Independently verify it by READING the cited code. Try to REFUTE it — default to real=false if the code already handles it, the claim is a stylistic nit, or it's not actually reachable by a user.

FILE: /app/(customer)/account/page.tsx
LOCATION: Line 156 – 'Next session' description text
RULE: 3
TITLE: Low contrast: text-ink-soft on bg-primary-tint in resume section
DETAIL: The resume/quick-start card uses `bg-primary-tint` (light teal #e4efec) with `text-ink-soft` (#6b6259 warm brown). This pairing has insufficient contrast for WCAG AA body text (4.5:1 minimum). The warm brown on cool light teal creates a visually pale result, particularly problematic for low-vision users. This is on line 156 in the 'Next session' label paragraph.
SUGGESTION: Change line 156 from `className="text-base text-ink-soft"` to `className="text-base text-ink"` (use the darker primary text color). Alternatively, adjust the card background or use a different color variable that has sufficient contrast with text-ink-soft if a lighter text is intentional.

Return real=true ONLY if this is a genuine, actionable accessibility/polish gap that a fix would meaningfully improve.
